summary: The study investigates the interfacial layer formed between HfO2 films grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD) using HfI4 and O2 as precursors and a silicon substrate. The interfacial layer is amorphous and composed of SiO2 mixed with a small amount of elemental Si. The interfacial layer forms primarily at the beginning of the ALD process and is influenced by deposition parameters such as temperature and precursor chemistry.
evidence: The interfacial layer was amorphous and contained SiO2 mixed with a small amount of elemental Si on the atomic level. The interfacial silicon oxide layer was mainly deposited at the beginning of the ALD process since its thickness was insensitive to the number of applied ALD cycles when increased from 50 to 1000. The HfO2 thin films were grown in a flow-type ALD reactor on Si(100) substrates at the temperatures 620 and 750°C.
